description: Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken is a beloved dish featuring incredibly crispy fried chicken coated in a sticky, sweet, and spicy gochujang-based sauce. This iconic Korean street food offers an irresistible balance of flavors and textures, making it a perfect treat for any occasion. Prepare to impress your taste buds with this authentic and satisfying recipe.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Pat chicken pieces very dry with paper towels. In a large bowl, season the chicken with salt, black pepper, ginger powder, garlic powder, and soju or mirin if using. Mix well and let it marinate for 10-15 minutes.

instructions.title: Make the Batter
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, whisk together potato starch, all-purpose flour, and baking powder. Gradually add cold water, mixing until you achieve a smooth, pancake-like batter. The consistency should be thick enough to coat the chicken without being too runny.

instructions.title: First Fry
instructions.text: Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 325F (160C). Dip each chicken piece into the batter, ensuring it's fully coated, then carefully place it into the hot oil. Fry in batches for about 6-8 minutes, or until lightly golden and cooked through. Remove chicken and place on a wire rack to drain. This is the first fry.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce
instructions.text: While the chicken rests, combine all Yangnyeom sauce ingredients in a small saucepan: gochujang, ketchup, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey or corn syrup, brown sugar, minced garlic, minced ginger, sesame oil, and water. Bring to a simmer over medium-low heat, stirring constantly until the sugar dissolves and the sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes. Set aside.

instructions.title: Second Fry
instructions.text: Increase the oil temperature to 350F (175C). Carefully return the pre-fried chicken to the hot oil for a second fry. Fry for another 3-5 minutes, or until deep golden brown and extra crispy. This double-frying method is key to achieving that signature Korean fried chicken crunch. Remove and drain on a wire rack.

instructions.title: Coat the Chicken
instructions.text: Immediately transfer the hot, crispy chicken into a large bowl. Pour the warm Yangnyeom sauce over the chicken and toss gently but quickly to ensure every piece is evenly coated. Work fast to maintain crispiness.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.text: Transfer the coated chicken to a serving platter. Garnish generously with toasted sesame seeds and chopped green onions. Serve immediately and enjoy the perfect balance of sweet, spicy, and savory flavors.

tips: For the crispiest chicken, ensure your oil temperature is consistent and perform the double-frying method as instructed. The first fry cooks the chicken, and the second fry makes it extra crispy.
Adjust the spice level of the Yangnyeom sauce by varying the amount of gochujang. For a sweeter sauce, add more honey or corn syrup.
Serve Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken immediately after coating to enjoy its optimal crispiness and the full flavor of the sauce. It pairs wonderfully with pickled radishes (mu ssam) and a cold beer.
article:
Craving that perfect balance of sweet, spicy, and savory crunch? Look no further than Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken, a culinary sensation that has captivated taste buds worldwide. More than just a dish, it's an experience – a symphony of textures and flavors that elevates humble fried chicken to an art form. From bustling streets of Seoul to upscale restaurants and home kitchens globally, Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken has become synonymous with deliciousness, representing the vibrant and innovative spirit of Korean cuisine. If you've ever wondered how to achieve that legendary crispiness and irresistible sauce, you're in the right place. Get ready to embark on a flavorful journey to master this iconic Korean chicken recipe.

## What is Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken?

Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken, often simply called "Yangnyeom Chicken," translates literally to "seasoned sauce chicken." This name perfectly encapsulates its essence: perfectly fried chicken pieces generously coated in a sticky, glossy, and intensely flavorful sauce. Unlike its American counterpart, which often focuses on a crispy breading and optional dipping sauces, Yangnyeom chicken’s identity is inextricably linked to its signature glaze.

The sauce is a complex masterpiece, typically featuring a base of gochujang (Korean chili paste), soy sauce, garlic, sugar or corn syrup, rice vinegar, and often a touch of sesame oil. The result is a harmonious blend of sweet, spicy, tangy, and savory notes that cling to every crackle of the double-fried chicken skin. The spice level can range from mildly sweet and tangy to a fiery kick, depending on the chef's preference and the amount of gochujang and gochugaru (Korean chili flakes) used. This unique sauce, combined with the incredibly light and airy crispness of the chicken, is what makes Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken an unforgettable treat.

## Ingredients for Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken

To create authentic Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken, you'll need a few key ingredients, some of which are staples in Korean pantries.

**For the Chicken:**
*   **Chicken:** 2-3 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (wings, drumettes, or thighs cut into smaller pieces work best).
*   **Marinade (Optional but Recommended):** 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp grated ginger, 1 tsp minced garlic, 1 tbsp mirin or rice wine, pinch of black pepper.
*   **Dredging/Coating:** 1 cup potato starch (preferred for crispiness) or cornstarch, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder (for extra crisp), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper.
*   **Frying Oil:** Enough neutral oil (canola, vegetable, peanut) for deep frying.

**For the Yangnyeom Sauce:**
*   **Gochujang:** 2-3 tbsp (Korean chili paste, adjust to your spice preference).
*   **Soy Sauce:** 2 tbsp.
*   **Sugar/Corn Syrup/Honey:** 2-3 tbsp (corn syrup gives the best glossy texture).
*   **Rice Vinegar:** 1 tbsp.
*   **Minced Garlic:** 2-3 cloves.
*   **Sesame Oil:** 1 tsp.
*   **Water or Chicken Broth:** 2-3 tbsp (to thin the sauce).
*   **Optional:** 1 tsp gochugaru (for extra heat), 1 tbsp ketchup (for added tang and sweetness).

**For Garnish:** Toasted sesame seeds, chopped green onions.

## Step-by-Step: Making Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken

Making Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken at home is a rewarding process. Follow these steps for crispy, saucy perfection:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Pat the chicken pieces thoroughly dry with paper towels – this is crucial for crispiness. If marinating, combine chicken with marinade ingredients and let sit for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator. After marinating, pat dry again.
2.  **Prepare the Coating:** In a large bowl, whisk together potato starch (or cornstarch), flour, baking powder, salt, and black pepper.
3.  **Coat the Chicken:** Dredge each piece of chicken in the dry coating mixture, ensuring it's fully covered. Shake off any excess. Place coated chicken on a wire rack.
4.  **First Fry:** Heat frying oil in a large pot or deep fryer to 325-350°F (160-175°C). Fry the chicken in batches, being careful not to overcrowd the pot. Fry for 6-8 minutes, or until cooked through, lightly golden, and no longer pink inside. Remove chicken and place on a wire rack to rest. This rest period allows the chicken to steam slightly and ensures a crispier second fry.
5.  **Prepare the Yangnyeom Sauce:** While the chicken rests, combine all Yangnyeom sauce ingredients in a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens slightly and becomes glossy (about 3-5 minutes). Keep warm.
6.  **Second Fry:** Increase the oil temperature to 375°F (190°C). Fry the chicken again in batches for another 2-4 minutes, or until deeply golden brown and incredibly crispy. This double-frying technique is the secret to the signature crunch.
7.  **Toss and Serve:** Immediately transfer the hot, crispy chicken directly into the warm Yangnyeom sauce. Toss quickly to coat all pieces evenly. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and chopped green onions. Serve hot.

## Tips for the Crispiest Yangnyeom Chicken

Achieving that legendary crunch requires a few key techniques:

*   **Double Frying is Essential:** This cannot be stressed enough. The first fry cooks the chicken, and the second, higher-temperature fry creates the super crispy exterior.
*   **Use Potato Starch:** While cornstarch works, potato starch creates a lighter, airier, and more shatteringly crisp coating that holds up better to the sauce.
*   **Add Baking Powder:** A small amount of baking powder in the coating mixture helps create tiny air bubbles, contributing to the chicken's incredible crispness.
*   **Pat Chicken Dry:** Moisture is the enemy of crispiness. Ensure your chicken is thoroughly patted dry before coating.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Fryer:** Frying in small batches maintains the oil temperature, preventing the chicken from steaming instead of frying.
*   **Rest Between Fries:** Allowing the chicken to rest on a wire rack between fries helps regulate its internal temperature and ensures a better texture.
*   **Toss Just Before Serving:** To maintain maximum crispness, toss the chicken in the sauce right before you eat it. The sauce will inevitably soften the crust over time.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken is a star on its own, but it shines even brighter with the right accompaniments.

*   **Pickled Radish (Mu-saengchae):** The quintessential pairing! The tangy, refreshing crunch of pickled radish cuts through the richness of the chicken beautifully.
*   **Rice:** A simple bowl of steamed white rice is perfect for soaking up any extra sauce.
*   **Kimchi:** The fermented spice of kimchi offers another fantastic counterpoint to the sweet and savory chicken.
*   **Beer (Chimaek):** The "chimaek" culture (chicken + maekju/beer) is legendary in Korea. A cold lager or light ale is the perfect beverage to wash down the deliciousness.
*   **Soju:** For those who prefer a stronger drink, a chilled bottle of soju also pairs wonderfully.
*   **Coleslaw or Corn Salad:** Creamy, cool side dishes can offer a nice textural and temperature contrast.

## Variations & FAQs

**Variations:**
*   **Less Spicy/Mild:** Reduce the gochujang and omit the gochugaru. You can increase sugar or honey for a sweeter profile.
*   **Extra Spicy:** Add more gochujang and a generous amount of gochugaru to the sauce.
*   **Garlic Soy:** For a completely different flavor, omit gochujang and create a sauce with more soy sauce, minced garlic, sugar, and a touch of black pepper.
*   **Honey Garlic:** A milder, sweeter variation using honey, soy sauce, and plenty of minced garlic.

**FAQs:**

*   **Can I make Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken ahead of time?** The sauce can be made a day or two in advance and reheated. However, for the best crispy texture, the chicken should be fried and tossed in sauce immediately before serving. Leftovers will be delicious but lose their signature crunch.
*   **What if I don't have gochujang?** While substitutes exist (like a mix of chili paste, sugar, and soy sauce), gochujang is crucial for the authentic flavor of Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken. It's highly recommended to seek it out in Asian grocery stores.
*   **Can I bake or air fry the chicken?** Yes, you can bake or air fry for a healthier option, but the texture will be different. It won't achieve the same light, airy crispness as deep-fried chicken, but it will still be delicious with the sauce.
*   **What's the difference between Yangnyeom and Ganjang chicken?** Yangnyeom chicken is characterized by its sweet, spicy, and tangy red sauce, while Ganjang chicken (or soy garlic chicken) features a savory, slightly sweet, and intensely garlicky soy-based sauce. Both are incredibly popular Korean fried chicken variations.

Yangnyeom Korean Fried Chicken is more than just a meal; it’s a celebration of flavor and texture. With its signature crispy crust and irresistible sweet-spicy-savory sauce, it’s a dish that promises to delight and satisfy. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to bring the authentic taste of Korea into your kitchen. Enjoy every crunchy, saucy bite!
